meta.title: Working together — Patrick Brant
meta.description: Three ways to work with Patrick Brant: expert witness and technical counsel, R&D advisory from catalyst to product, and ventures and research.

sections.label: Working together
sections.quote: A material is chemistry <t>until it ships.</t>
sections.sub: Three ways in: a patent matter, a product that has to scale, a venture or a research question.

sections.label: Where it begins
sections.title: Where the conversation <t>usually begins.</t>
items: A patent dispute over a polyolefin, a catalyst or a film, and counsel who need an expert who has invented in that field.
A product that works in the pilot plant and not in the world-scale reactor.
A film, membrane or adhesive that fails at the customer, and nobody can say why.
A composite or nanocomposite that needs coupling chemistry to hold.
An R&D team that needs a mentor who has carried programmes from idea to commercial product.
A symposium or conference that needs someone to shape the programme.

sections.label: Three ways in
sections.title: Three ways <t>to work together.</t>
sections.lede: Each one a chapter of forty years, still open.

cards.label: Expert witness & technical counsel · Patent counsel & legal teams
cards.title: Who has invented in this field?
cards.desc: Olefin polymerisation catalysis, structure–property relationships and product design, explained to a tribunal by someone named on more than 150 US patents and thirty-seven years inside the company that commercialised the chemistry.

cards.label: R&D advisory · R&D leaders, converters & brand owners
cards.title: Why does it work in the pilot plant and not in the reactor?
cards.desc: From catalyst to product: synthesis and functionalisation, scale-up, plant and customer troubleshooting, and the structure–property and rheology work that decides whether a material performs.

cards.label: Ventures & research · Founders, investors & universities
cards.title: What holds a composite together?
cards.desc: Molecular Joinery, LLC, for composite and nanocomposite design and coupling-agent chemistry; research with the University of Houston and Baylor University; ROMP chemistry for the oil field.

sections.label: Through Molecular Joinery
sections.sub: Founded in Seabrook, Texas: proprietary composite and nanocomposite design, coupling-agent chemistry and coatings. Current interests include high-throughput methods for grafting polymers to hard substrates and Grubbs-type ROMP chemistry for plugging abandoned wells and backing up blow-out control offshore.
